claims.text: The initial material is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Selective laser sintering can introduce controlled porosity into HfMoTaTiZr.
Introducing controlled porosity will reduce the density of HfMoTaTiZr.
The selectively laser-sintered porous material will retain a strong, interconnected matrix phase.
Retention of a strong, interconnected matrix phase will prevent significant loss of mechanical properties despite the introduced porosity.
The intervention will decrease density relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Room-temperature strength will be maintained or only slightly reduced relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Elevated-temperature strength will be maintained relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The hypothesis is intended to apply from room temperature through 1000 °C.
The stated loading boundary includes tensile and compressive loading.
The extent of porosity may affect the mechanical properties.
Oxidation may affect the material at elevated temperatures.
The proposed experiment compares as-cast and selectively laser-sintered HfMoTaTiZr at room temperature and 1000 °C using density, tensile strength, compressive strength, and hardness measurements.
A strength decrease greater than 10% at either room temperature or 1000 °C relative to the as-cast sample will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The headline claims no compromise in mechanical properties, while the predicted outcome permits slightly reduced room-temperature strength and the falsification rule permits strength losses of up to 10%.
